    Add OpenAlex impact fields to any corpus

    Source: R/enrich-openalex-impact.R
    sm_enrich_openalex_impact.Rd

    Looks the works of a corpus up on OpenAlex by identifier and adds OpenAlex's impact fields: the field-weighted citation impact (fwci), the citation percentile (citation_percentile, 0 to 1, with the flags is_top_10pct and is_top_1pct), the date of these values (citations_as_of) and the yearly citation counts (the corpus element citations_by_year). The corpus can come from any source, such as Web of Science files or sm_corpus_from_tables(); only identifiers are sent.

    Usage

    sm_enrich_openalex_impact(
  corpus,
  by = c("openalex_id", "doi"),
  batch_size = 50L,
  api_key = Sys.getenv("OPENALEX_API_KEY"),
  verbose = TRUE,
  call = rlang::caller_env()
)

    Arguments

    corpus

    An sm_corpus.

    by

    The identifiers to look works up by, in order of preference: one or both of "openalex_id" and "doi". The default tries the OpenAlex id first and the DOI for works without one, as in corpora from Web of Science files, whose openalex_id is NA.

    batch_size

    Number of identifiers per request, from 1 to 100 (default 50). Larger values are lowered to 100 with a message.

    api_key

    OpenAlex API key. Read from the OPENALEX_API_KEY environment variable by default; see "API key and rate limits".

    verbose

    Print progress messages?

    call

    Caller environment for error reporting.

    Value

    The corpus with the works columns fwci, citation_percentile, is_top_10pct, is_top_1pct and citations_as_of (see sm_corpus()), the element citations_by_year and a provenance row for each work found. The columns and the element are added even when OpenAlex has none of the works looked up (with NA and no rows where the corpus had none). A corpus without works, or without works that have an identifier, is returned unchanged.

    Details

    Each work is looked up by the first identifier of by that it has: its OpenAlex id (works$openalex_id, shortened to the W number) or its DOI (normalised on both sides, so https://doi.org/ prefixes and case do not matter). Works without either are counted and left as they are. A DOI that contains , or | cannot be written into an OpenAlex filter; such works are left out and counted too. The identifiers are sent in batches of batch_size (at most 100, the number of values an OpenAlex filter takes), with only the fields needed (select). When OpenAlex has several records for one DOI, the record with the most yearly citations is used, then the one with the lowest OpenAlex id.

    The fields are joined with sm_materialise() (overwrite = TRUE). All five values of a work found come from its OpenAlex record, NA where the record has none, so a new run replaces the values of an earlier run or of another source, and the values, their date (citations_as_of) and the yearly counts of a work always belong to one record. The works not found keep their values. Only these five works columns change; cited_by_count and the other columns keep the values of their source. The citations_by_year rows of every work found are replaced by the counts OpenAlex has now; the rows of the other works stay. metadata$last_refresh is not changed.

    Every work found gets a provenance row with the source "openalex_impact", its OpenAlex id in source_id_external, a short description of the call in query and the kind "enrichment", so sm_rebuild_from_cert() never replays the step as a search. Neither the API key nor any request URL or filter is stored.

    On HTTP 429 (the request budget is used up) the function stops at once and joins nothing, not even the batches fetched before: a partial enrichment would compare works with OpenAlex values against works without them. The error (class scimapR_openalex_rate_limit) names the reset time, the remaining budget OpenAlex reports and the key setting. Any other failed request stops it too (class scimapR_openalex_failed).

    API key and rate limits

    OpenAlex expects a free API key. Requests without one share one small daily budget with everyone on the same network address; once it is used up, OpenAlex answers HTTP 429 (too many requests) until the budget resets at midnight UTC. Set the key in the OPENALEX_API_KEY environment variable (for example in ~/.Renviron) or pass it as api_key. It is sent in the Authorization header, never in the URL, and it is stored nowhere in the corpus.

    On HTTP 429 the function stops at once with an error of class scimapR_openalex_rate_limit instead of waiting: the message gives the reset time and the remaining budget that OpenAlex reports (the fields reset_at and remaining of the condition) and says whether a key was sent. Only a wait of up to two seconds (OpenAlex also limits requests per second) is waited out, once. Other failed requests stop with class scimapR_openalex_failed; both classes inherit from scimapR_openalex_error. With engine = "openalexR" the openalexR package (version 3.1.1 or later) sends the requests: it gets the key too and its own retries are switched off, but it does not pass on the response headers, so the reset time and the budget are not known.

    See also

    sm_fetch_openalex(), sm_citation_window()

    Other enrichers: sm_enrich_altmetric(), sm_enrich_concepts(), sm_enrich_opencitations(), sm_enrich_orcid(), sm_enrich_retraction(), sm_enrich_ror(), sm_enrich_specter(), sm_enrich_unpaywall()

    Examples

    if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
fix <- readRDS(sm_example_files("example_realuse_corpus.rds"))
fix <- sm_enrich_openalex_impact(fix, by = "doi")
sm_citation_window(fix, window = 3)
} # }
